parent_models.justification: The Koopman dynamics model can be seen as an extension of linear dynamical systems, where Markovian models provide a general framework for modeling state transitions over time. The Koopman approach can incorporate more expressive dynamics retaining a structure related to processes that may be Markovian in nature.

While Koopman dynamics models focus on system dynamics using linear operators, agent-based models are a general class concerned with dynamic simulation of autonomous agents, reflecting a broader interest in dynamics.

closest_parent_model.justification: Koopman dynamics extend the concept of Markov processes by projecting nonlinear dynamics into a linear framework, aligning closely with the principles underlying Markovian models of state transitions.

child_models.justification: The 'temporal koopman networks' is a specialized approach within the broader Koopman dynamics model family, focusing on networked systems with temporal dimensions, thereby being a child model.

closest_child_model.justification: Being a specialized architecture focusing on temporal dynamics using Koopman operators, 'temporal koopman networks' represent the most direct application under the Koopman dynamics model framework.
